qa_pairs.question: What is Isoniazid?
qa_pairs.answer:
**Isoniazid (H/INH) - Comprehensive Information:**

**DOSING:**
• Adults: 5 mg/kg (Maximum: 300 mg daily)
• Pediatric: 10 mg/kg
• Administration: Once daily, preferably on empty stomach (30-60 min before meals)

**MECHANISM OF ACTION:**
• Classification: Bactericidal - kills actively growing TB bacteria
• How it works: Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis in bacterial cell wall
• Role in TB treatment: Essential component of standard regimen

**SIDE EFFECTS & MONITORING:**
• Common side effects: Peripheral neuropathy, Hepatitis, Drug-induced lupus, Seizures (overdose)
• Prevention/Management: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) 40-150 mg daily to prevent neuropathy
• Monitoring required: Baseline and monthly LFTs, monitor for jaundice/hepatitis symptoms, assess for peripheral neuropathy
• When to stop: Immediately if severe reactions occur

**SPECIAL POPULATIONS:**
• Pregnancy: SAFE - Category A, continue treatment during pregnancy
• Breastfeeding: SAFE - compatible with breastfeeding
• Renal impairment: [Specific guidance based on drug]
• Hepatic impairment: Use with caution, monitor LFTs

**CLINICAL PEARLS:**
• No color changes (urine remains normal)
• Never use as monotherapy
• Compliance critical - missing doses leads to resistance
• Part of standard DOTS regimen

**SOURCE:** South African DoH TB Training Manual 2024, Pakistan NTP Guidelines 2024

qa_pairs.question: What is Rifampicin?
qa_pairs.answer:
**Rifampicin (R/RIF) - Comprehensive Information:**

**DOSING:**
• Adults: 10 mg/kg (Maximum: 600 mg daily)
• Pediatric: 15 mg/kg
• Administration: Once daily, preferably on empty stomach (30-60 min before meals)

**MECHANISM OF ACTION:**
• Classification: Bactericidal - most potent TB drug, sterilizing activity
• How it works: Inhibits bacterial RNA polymerase, preventing RNA synthesis
• Role in TB treatment: Essential component of standard regimen

**SIDE EFFECTS & MONITORING:**
• Common side effects: Orange-red discoloration of body fluids (normal), Hepatitis, Flu-like syndrome, Drug interactions (many)
• Prevention/Management: Reassure patient about orange color (normal finding), Monitor LFTs
• Monitoring required: Baseline and monthly LFTs, monitor for hepatotoxicity, check drug interactions, warn about orange discoloration
• When to stop: Immediately if severe reactions occur

**SPECIAL POPULATIONS:**
• Pregnancy: SAFE - Category C, benefits outweigh risks
• Breastfeeding: SAFE - compatible with breastfeeding
• Renal impairment: [Specific guidance based on drug]
• Hepatic impairment: Use with caution, monitor LFTs

**CLINICAL PEARLS:**
• Orange-red urine, sweat, tears, saliva (NORMAL - reassure patient)
• Never use as monotherapy
• Compliance critical - missing doses leads to resistance
• Part of standard DOTS regimen

**SOURCE:** South African DoH TB Training Manual 2024, Pakistan NTP Guidelines 2024

qa_pairs.question: What is Pyrazinamide?
qa_pairs.answer:
**Pyrazinamide (Z/PZA) - Comprehensive Information:**

**DOSING:**
• Adults: 25 mg/kg (Maximum: 2000 mg daily)
• Pediatric: 35 mg/kg
• Administration: Once daily, preferably on empty stomach (30-60 min before meals)

**MECHANISM OF ACTION:**
• Classification: Bactericidal in acidic pH - sterilizing activity
• How it works: Disrupts membrane energetics and transport functions
• Role in TB treatment: Essential component of standard regimen

**SIDE EFFECTS & MONITORING:**
• Common side effects: Hepatotoxicity, Arthralgia (joint pain), Hyperuricemia, Gout, Photosensitivity
• Prevention/Management: NSAIDs/Aspirin for joint pain, Monitor uric acid levels, Adequate hydration
• Monitoring required: Baseline and monthly LFTs, uric acid levels, monitor for joint pain and hepatotoxicity
• When to stop: Immediately if severe reactions occur

**SPECIAL POPULATIONS:**
• Pregnancy: SAFE per WHO 2024 - benefits outweigh risks
• Breastfeeding: SAFE - compatible with breastfeeding
• Renal impairment: [Specific guidance based on drug]
• Hepatic impairment: Use with caution, monitor LFTs

**CLINICAL PEARLS:**
• No color changes
• Never use as monotherapy
• Compliance critical - missing doses leads to resistance
• Part of standard DOTS regimen

**SOURCE:** South African DoH TB Training Manual 2024, Pakistan NTP Guidelines 2024

qa_pairs.question: What is Ethambutol?
qa_pairs.answer:
**Ethambutol (E/EMB) - Comprehensive Information:**

**DOSING:**
• Adults: 15 mg/kg (Maximum: 1200 mg daily)
• Pediatric: 20 mg/kg
• Administration: Once daily, preferably on empty stomach (30-60 min before meals)

**MECHANISM OF ACTION:**
• Classification: Bacteriostatic - prevents resistance development
• How it works: Inhibits arabinosyl transferases, blocking cell wall synthesis
• Role in TB treatment: Essential component of standard regimen

**SIDE EFFECTS & MONITORING:**
• Common side effects: Optic neuritis (vision loss), Color blindness (red-green), Peripheral neuropathy
• Prevention/Management: Monthly visual acuity and color vision testing, Stop immediately if vision changes
• Monitoring required: Baseline and monthly visual acuity testing, color vision assessment, educate patient to report vision changes immediately
• When to stop: Immediately if severe reactions occur

**SPECIAL POPULATIONS:**
• Pregnancy: Category C - use with caution, benefits must outweigh risks
• Breastfeeding: SAFE - compatible with breastfeeding
• Renal impairment: [Specific guidance based on drug]
• Hepatic impairment: Use with caution, monitor LFTs

**CLINICAL PEARLS:**
• No color changes
• Never use as monotherapy
• Compliance critical - missing doses leads to resistance
• Part of standard DOTS regimen

**SOURCE:** South African DoH TB Training Manual 2024, Pakistan NTP Guidelines 2024

qa_pairs.question: How do I manage New Smear-Positive Pulmonary TB?
qa_pairs.answer:
**Clinical Scenario: New Smear-Positive Pulmonary TB**

**PRESENTATION:**
Patient: 28-year-old male
Symptoms: Cough for 6 weeks, hemoptysis, night sweats, 8 kg weight loss
Examination: Fever 38.5°C, cachexia, reduced breath sounds right upper lobe
Investigation: Sputum GeneXpert MTB detected, RIF sensitive

**DIAGNOSTIC APPROACH:**
1. Confirm diagnosis: Sputum smear-positive, GeneXpert positive
2. Classify: New case, drug-sensitive pulmonary TB
3. Check HIV status: Offer HIV testing
4. Assess severity: Moderate-severe based on symptoms
5. Rule out complications: Chest X-ray for cavitation

**MANAGEMENT PLAN:**
**IMMEDIATE ACTIONS:**
1. Start standard DS-TB treatment: 2HRZE/4HR
2. Initiate DOTS supervision
3. Isolate patient (if hospitalized) or educate on cough hygiene
4. Notify TB program (TB01 form)
5. Screen household contacts

**TREATMENT REGIMEN:**
• Intensive Phase (2 months): HRZE daily
  - Weight-based FDC dosing
  - Directly observed therapy
• Continuation Phase (4 months): HR daily
  - Continue DOTS
  - Monthly follow-up

**MONITORING:**
• Sputum at month 2, 5, 6
• Monthly clinical assessment
• Monitor for side effects
• Ensure adherence

**PATIENT EDUCATION:**
• Explain 6-month treatment duration
• Emphasize adherence importance
• Discuss side effects
• Cough hygiene and infection control

**EXPECTED OUTCOME:**
• Sputum conversion by month 2: 85%+
• Treatment success: >90%
• Cure expected with full adherence

**MONITORING & FOLLOW-UP:**
• Regular clinical assessment
• Appropriate laboratory monitoring
• Treatment adherence support
• Contact tracing and screening

**PATIENT EDUCATION:**
• Explain diagnosis and treatment plan
• Emphasize importance of adherence
• Discuss expected duration and outcomes
• Address concerns and questions

**EXPECTED OUTCOME:**
With proper treatment and adherence, excellent prognosis expected.

**SOURCE:** Evidence-based clinical guidelines 2024
